prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Immediate first steps
- Fiscal stability via strict spending rules; 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week; new Border Security Command; establish publicly owned Great British Energy; antisocial behaviour crackdown with more neighbourhood police and youth hubs; recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects.

Economy, tax and business
- Fiscal rules: current budget to balance; debt falling by year five; OBR oversight of fiscal events.
- No rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close private equity “carried interest” loophole; strengthen HMRC against avoidance.
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing and annual investment allowance; replace business rates in England.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen); pension consolidation and review to boost UK investment.
- Industrial Strategy Council (statutory); sector plans (e.g., automotive, life sciences, creative); Regulatory Innovation Office; support for AI with binding rules on frontier models and ban on sexually explicit deepfakes; 10-year R&D budgets; National Data Library.
- Small business: tackle late payments; reform British Business Bank and procurement access; strengthen Post Office network and Horizon justice.

Infrastructure, transport and connectivity
- 10-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform for major projects; full gigabit and 5G coverage by 2030.
- Roads maintenance including 1m potholes/year; support EV transition (restore 2030 ICE phase-out, charging rollout).
- Rail: bring passenger services into public ownership as contracts expire; create Great British Railways; expand rail freight; stronger passenger watchdog.
- Buses: franchising powers for local leaders; lift ban on municipal ownership; integrated local transport; support for sustainable aviation fuels and airspace modernisation.

Housing and planning
- Build 1.5m homes; restore mandatory targets; fund more planning officers; brownfield-first plus strategic “grey belt” release under “golden rules”; new towns; cross-boundary planning; CPO reform.
- Expand social and affordable housing; review Right to Buy discounts; first-time buyer priority; permanent mortgage guarantee; improve standards and nutrient neutrality solutions.

Devolution and local government
- Landmark devolution in England over transport, skills, housing, employment support; Local Growth Plans; multi-year council settlements; audit overhaul. Collaboration with devolved governments; structural funds devolved.

Immigration and borders
- Border Security Command; end Rwanda scheme; hire caseworkers to clear backlog; end hotel use; new returns unit (+1,000 staff); seek EU security agreement.
- Reform points-based system; link migration to skills plans; enforcement against exploitative employers.

Work and rights
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; end fire-and-rehire; day-one rights to sick pay, parental leave and protection from unfair dismissal; Single Enforcement Body.
- Minimum wage to reflect living costs; remove age bands.

Law, order and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; knife crime plan (mandatory interventions; ban certain blades; online sales controls); Young Futures hubs.
- Specialist rape units and courts; improved vetting and standards; expanded fraud strategy; prisons capacity; reoffending reduction; probation governance review; address historical injustices.

Energy, climate, nature and farming
- Clean power by 2030: expand wind/solar; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; extend existing nuclear and proceed with Hinkley/Sizewell C/SMRs; maintain gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; no fracking/coal; strengthen windfall levy; Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and scale local power; grid upgrade; British Jobs Bonus.
- Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; carbon border adjustment; green finance transition plans for regulated firms.
- Water: tougher regulation, automatic fines, block bonuses for polluters; new river walks and forests; stronger animal welfare; public sector food procurement target for local/high-standard supply.

Health, care and public health
- Cut waiting lists (pooling lists; evening/weekend sessions; independent sector capacity); long-term workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; enhanced NHS app; maternity safety; regulate managers; implement Cass Review recommendations.
- Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face guarantee; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; Neighbourhood Health Centres pilots.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing).
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; “home first” model.
- Mental health: 8,500 additional staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; curb youth vaping marketing; restrict junk food ads to children; online safety and gambling reforms; reduce health inequalities.

Education, skills and culture
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; review parental leave; unique child identifier; 6,500 teachers; restore support staff negotiating body; early maths and language focus; leadership programme; inspection reform (report cards); curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusion; free primary breakfast clubs; school mental health support.
- Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy to Growth and Skills Levy; HE funding and access reforms.
- Expand access to arts, music and sport; football regulator; ticket resale protections; end private school VAT/business rates relief to fund state education.

Governance and democracy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; stronger ministerial standards; restrict MPs’ consultancy roles; Commons modernisation.
- Lords reform: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; stronger standards; consult on replacement. Votes at 16; improve voter registration and ID rules; strengthen donation rules.

Foreign, defence and development
- NATO commitment; nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% GDP defence spend; Armed Forces Covenant in law; Armed Forces Commissioner; scrap visa fees for eligible non-UK veterans; defence industrial strategy.
- Ukraine support; AUKUS; calibrated approach to China; remain in ECHR.
- Post-Brexit EU relationship: improve trade (veterinary agreement, MRAs), security pact, support touring artists; targeted trade deals (incl. India); WTO/CPTPP engagement; global minimum tax.
- Clean Power Alliance internationally; rebuild development capability; restore 0.7% aid when fiscal conditions allow; focus on poverty, climate, debt, women and girls, conflict prevention, climate finance.
